categories.label: First purees
categories.description: Very smooth, single-ingredient purees, including iron-rich first foods.

categories.label: Thicker and mashed
categories.description: Thicker purees, fork-mashed foods and gentle first allergens.

categories.label: Lumps and finger foods
categories.description: Lumpy textures and soft finger foods your baby can pick up.

categories.label: Toddler meals
categories.description: Soft, chopped family-style meals, cut into pieces no bigger than about 1/2 inch.

categories.label: One pot for family and baby
categories.description: Cook once for the whole family: scoop baby’s portion out before seasoning, then serve it as finger food or a mash.

recipes.title: Iron-fortified oat cereal
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] A smooth, iron-rich first food ready in two minutes.

familyMeal.note: Oats for everyone: stir up your overnight oats while baby has their cereal.

ingredients: 1 to 2 tbsp iron-fortified oat infant cereal
Breast milk, formula or water to mix
steps: Stir the cereal with enough breast milk, formula or water to make a thin, smooth mix.
Serve from a spoon. Thicken it a little as your baby gets used to eating.
tips: Never put cereal in a bottle.
Rotate oat, barley and multigrain cereals rather than only rice cereal.
Some oat cereals are processed with wheat; check the label if you avoid gluten.

recipes.title: Sweet potato puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Naturally sweet and silky; freezes in handy cubes.

familyMeal.note: Roast a sweet potato on the same sheet pan, then puree baby's portion with no seasoning.

ingredients: Breast milk, formula or water to thin
steps: Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into even chunks.
Steam or boil for 15 to 20 minutes, until soft enough to mash easily with a fork.
Puree until completely smooth. Thin with breast milk, formula or water until very smooth.
tips: No salt, sugar or seasoning needed.
Freeze extra in ice-cube trays, then move the cubes to labeled, dated bags and use within 3 months.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly, and check for signs of spoilage before serving.

recipes.title: Smooth chicken puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] An easy way to offer iron and zinc from the very start.

familyMeal.note: Simmer a little plain chicken for baby while the family's seasoned chicken cooks.

ingredients: 8 oz boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast
Water, breast milk or formula to thin
steps: Trim off any fat, then cut the chicken into small pieces.
Simmer in water for about 15 minutes, until cooked through to 165°F. Keep the cooking water.
Blend with some of the cooking water until completely smooth, with no stringy bits. Thin with breast milk, formula or water until very smooth.
tips: Mix with a vegetable puree your baby already eats if the texture is too thick on its own.
Refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 2 to 6 months for best quality.
Halal and kosher depend on the chicken you buy; check the label.

recipes.title: Ripe pear puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] A gentle, sweet first fruit.

familyMeal.note: Top your overnight oats with chopped pear and puree the rest for baby.

steps: Peel, core and chop the pears.
Steam for 5 to 8 minutes until very soft.
Puree until smooth. Thin with breast milk, formula or water until very smooth.
tips: Freeze extra in ice-cube trays, then move the cubes to labeled, dated bags and use within 3 months.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly, and check for signs of spoilage before serving.

recipes.title: Smooth avocado and pear mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Creamy avocado with naturally sweet pear, blended silky smooth.

familyMeal.note: Mash a little extra avocado for your own toast while baby has theirs.

ingredients: Water, breast milk or formula to thin
steps: Peel and core the pear, cut it into pieces, and steam for 5 to 7 minutes until fork-tender.
Halve the avocado and scoop out the flesh.
Blend the pear and avocado until completely smooth.
Thin with a little water, breast milk or formula until runny and smooth.
tips: Offer each food on its own a few times before you mix them together.
Serve fresh. Avocado browns once cut; store leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge and use within a day.
Freeze the pear puree in cubes on its own, and mix in fresh avocado on the day.

recipes.title: Roasted sweet potato and apple mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Roasting brings out the natural sweetness of sweet potato and apple.

familyMeal.note: Roast an extra sweet potato for your breakfast hash tomorrow.

ingredients: 1 sweet apple, like Honeycrisp or Gala
Water, breast milk or formula to thin
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Prick the sweet potato a few times with a fork. Peel, core and chop the apple.
Roast the whole sweet potato and the apple pieces on a baking sheet for 25 to 30 minutes, until both are very soft. A larger sweet potato may need longer.
Scoop the sweet potato out of its skin and throw the skin away.
Blend the sweet potato and apple until silky smooth, thinning with water, breast milk or formula as needed.
tips: Offer each food on its own a few times before you mix them together.
Freeze in cubes and use within 3 months; refrigerate for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Butternut squash and chicken puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Tender squash and chicken, blended velvety smooth, for iron and protein.

familyMeal.note: Set aside a little plain chicken for baby before seasoning the family’s.

ingredients: 1 cup cubed butternut squash, fresh or frozen
1/4 cup cooked chicken breast or thigh, chopped (cooked to 165°F with no salt)
Water, breast milk or formula to thin
steps: Steam the squash until very tender.
Add the squash and chicken to a blender or food processor.
Add a generous splash of water, breast milk or formula to help the blades break down the chicken.
Blend on high until completely smooth, with no stringy bits.
tips: Skip store-bought broth, even low-sodium; it still adds salt babies don’t need.
Chicken thigh has more iron than breast, so it’s a good choice if you have it.
Freeze in cubes and use within 2 to 6 months for best quality; refrigerate for 3 to 4 days.
Halal and kosher depend on the chicken you buy; check the label.

recipes.title: Creamy apple-cinnamon baby oatmeal
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Iron-fortified oatmeal with smooth applesauce and a tiny pinch of cinnamon.

familyMeal.note: Make a pot of apple cinnamon porridge for yourself while baby has theirs.

ingredients: 1/4 cup breast milk, formula or water
steps: Gently warm the liquid. Warm breast milk or formula in a bowl of warm water, never in the microwave and never boiled.
Stir the warm liquid into the oatmeal until smooth and creamy.
Stir in the applesauce and a tiny pinch of cinnamon.
tips: Make it fresh each time, and throw away what your baby doesn’t eat.
Never put cereal in a bottle.
Some oat cereals are processed with wheat; check the label if you avoid gluten.

recipes.title: Smooth avocado puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Creamy, no-cook avocado, full of healthy fats.

familyMeal.note: Mash the other half of the avocado onto your own toast.

ingredients: 1 to 2 tsp breast milk, formula or water
steps: Scoop the avocado into a bowl and mash well with a fork.
Blend or whisk with the liquid until completely smooth, with no lumps.
tips: Serve fresh; cut avocado turns brown quickly. Keep leftovers covered in the fridge and use within a day.

recipes.title: Steamed carrot puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] A smooth, naturally sweet first vegetable.

familyMeal.note: Steam extra carrots and add them to your own lentil soup.

ingredients: Water, breast milk or formula to thin
steps: Peel the carrot and slice it into thin rounds.
Steam for 10 to 12 minutes, until very soft.
Blend until completely smooth. Thin with a little water, breast milk or formula until runny and smooth.
tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Smooth banana mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] No cooking needed: ripe banana mashed until smooth.

familyMeal.note: Blend the rest of the banana into your own smoothie.

ingredients: Breast milk, formula or water to thin (optional)
steps: Peel the banana and mash it well with a fork until no lumps remain.
Thin with a little breast milk, formula or water if needed.
tips: Serve fresh; mashed banana browns quickly.

recipes.title: Steamed apple puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Sweet apple, steamed soft and blended smooth.

familyMeal.note: Have the rest of the apple with peanut butter as your own snack.

ingredients: 1 sweet apple, such as Gala or Fuji
steps: Peel, core and chop the apple.
Steam for 8 to 10 minutes, until tender.
Blend until completely smooth, adding a little of the steaming water as needed.
tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Steamed butternut squash puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Velvety squash, rich in vitamins A and C.

familyMeal.note: Steam extra squash to add to your own stew.

ingredients: Water, breast milk or formula to thin
steps: Steam the squash for 12 to 15 minutes, until very soft.
Blend until completely smooth. Thin with a little water, breast milk or formula until runny and smooth.
tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Steamed pumpkin puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Smooth, comforting pumpkin, fresh or from a can.

familyMeal.note: Use the rest of the pumpkin in your own soup or curry.

ingredients: 1 cup peeled fresh pumpkin cubes, or canned 100% pumpkin
steps: Fresh pumpkin: steam the cubes for about 15 minutes, until tender, then blend until smooth.
Canned pumpkin: warm it gently with a splash of water.
tips: Check the can says 100% pumpkin; pumpkin pie filling has added sweeteners and spices.
Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Steamed zucchini puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] A very mild first green vegetable.

familyMeal.note: Steam a little zucchini for baby while you make your zucchini noodles.

steps: Trim the ends and chop the zucchini.
Steam for 6 to 8 minutes, until tender.
Blend until smooth.
tips: Zucchini is watery; if the puree is too runny, stir in a little infant cereal to thicken it.
Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Homemade oatmeal puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Finely ground oats cooked into a smooth, creamy first grain.

familyMeal.note: Stir up your overnight oats while baby has theirs.

ingredients: Breast milk or formula to thin (optional)
steps: Grind the oats into a fine flour in a blender.
Cook the oat flour in the water over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring constantly, until smooth and creamy.
Let it cool, then stir in a little breast milk or formula if you like.
tips: Homemade oats don’t have added iron. Iron-fortified infant cereal is an easy way to add iron at this age.
Some oats are processed with wheat; check the label if you avoid gluten.
Make it fresh, and throw away what your baby doesn’t eat.

recipes.title: Pear and banana blend
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Soft pear and banana, blended silky smooth.

familyMeal.note: Slice the rest of the pear into your own salad.

steps: Peel and core the pear, then steam it for about 5 minutes to soften.
Blend the pear and banana until silky smooth.
tips: Offer each food on its own a few times before you mix them together.
Serve fresh; banana browns quickly.

recipes.title: Carrot and butternut squash puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] A bright orange blend of carrot and squash.

familyMeal.note: Steam extra carrots for baby before you stir-fry the family’s.

ingredients: Water, breast milk or formula to thin
steps: Peel and chop the carrot and squash.
Steam together for 12 to 15 minutes, until completely tender.
Blend until smooth. Thin with a little water, breast milk or formula until runny and smooth.
tips: Offer each food on its own a few times before you mix them together.
Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Zucchini and sweet potato puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Mild zucchini balanced with naturally sweet sweet potato.

familyMeal.note: Roast extra sweet potato for your own quinoa bowls.

steps: Peel the sweet potato and chop both vegetables.
Steam together for about 12 minutes, until tender.
Blend until completely smooth.
tips: Offer each food on its own a few times before you mix them together.
Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Avocado and banana mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] No cooking, just a fork and two ripe fruits.

familyMeal.note: Mash extra avocado for baby before you add lemon, pepper or chili to yours.

steps: Mash the avocado and banana together with a fork.
Leave it a little textured, or add breast milk or formula to loosen.
tips: Make it fresh; avocado browns quickly.
Offer each fruit on its own first, a few days apart, before combining.

recipes.title: Red lentil and carrot mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Plant iron plus vitamin C in one pot.

familyMeal.note: Scoop out baby's lentils and carrots before you add the broth, garlic and tomatoes, then mash.

steps: Simmer the lentils and carrots in the water for 20 to 25 minutes, until both are very soft.
Mash with a fork or pulse briefly for a thick, slightly textured mash. Add water if needed.
tips: No salt or stock cubes; they add sodium.
Refrigerate for 3 to 4 days, or freeze portions and use within 2 to 3 months for best quality.

recipes.title: Soft egg mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] A simple way to introduce egg, fully cooked.

familyMeal.note: Hard-boil an extra egg for baby while your muffin cups bake.

ingredients: Breast milk or formula to loosen
steps: Hard-boil the egg for 10 to 12 minutes, until the yolk and white are completely firm.
Cool, peel and mash finely with a fork, adding breast milk or formula until soft and moist.
tips: Offer egg on a day with no other new foods, and watch for any reaction.
Once tolerated, keep egg in the diet regularly. About 1/3 of an egg is a typical portion.
If you're worried about egg allergy, talk to your pediatrician first.

recipes.title: Peanut oat cereal
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Thinned peanut butter stirred into cereal, the safe way to offer peanut.

familyMeal.note: Same flavors: make your peanut butter porridge, and thin a little peanut butter into baby's cereal.

ingredients: Warm breast milk, formula or water
steps: Stir the peanut butter into a little warm liquid until fully dissolved, with no lumps.
Mix in the cereal to a smooth, spoonable texture.
tips: Never offer chunks or spoonfuls of peanut butter; they're a choking hazard.
If your baby has severe eczema or an egg allergy, talk to your pediatrician before offering peanut.
Some oat cereals are processed with wheat; check the label if you avoid gluten.

recipes.title: Yogurt and blueberry swirl
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Plain whole-milk yogurt with a fruity swirl and no added sugar.

familyMeal.note: Make your parfait with the same berries; mash baby's well, as whole blueberries are a choking hazard.

steps: Simmer the blueberries with a splash of water for 5 minutes until they burst, then mash well and cool.
Swirl the mashed berries into the yogurt.
tips: Whole blueberries are a choking hazard at this age; always mash or cook them down.
Yogurt is fine before 12 months, but cow's milk as a drink waits until then.

recipes.title: Steamed apple and pear with cinnamon
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Naturally sweet and gentle, with a tiny pinch of cinnamon.

familyMeal.note: Steam extra apple to stir into your own cinnamon porridge.

ingredients: 1 small apple, peeled, cored and chopped
1 ripe pear, peeled, cored and chopped
steps: Steam the apple and pear in a covered steamer basket over boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes, until completely fork-tender.
Blend with the cinnamon until smooth, or mash with a fork if your baby is practicing textures.
Let it cool before serving.
tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Sweet potato and carrot mash with olive oil
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] A thick, creamy mash full of beta-carotene, with a little olive oil.

familyMeal.note: Steam a little extra sweet potato for your breakfast hash.

ingredients: 1 small sweet potato, peeled and diced
steps: Steam or boil the sweet potato and carrot for 12 to 15 minutes, until very tender.
Drain and transfer to a bowl.
Add the olive oil and mash until smooth and creamy. Let it cool before serving.
tips: Thin with a little water, breast milk or formula if it’s too thick.
Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Oatmeal and blueberry porridge
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Soft oats with warm mashed blueberries.

familyMeal.note: Make a jar of berry overnight oats for yourself tomorrow.

ingredients: 2 tbsp quick or rolled oats (ground a little for a smoother texture)
1/4 cup water, breast milk or formula
steps: Cook the oats in the water in a small pot over medium-low heat for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring often, until thick and soft.
Warm the blueberries gently until soft, then mash them well with a fork so no whole berries are left.
Stir the blueberries into the oatmeal. If you’re using breast milk or formula, stir it in now, off the heat. Let it cool before serving.
tips: Whole blueberries are a choking hazard; always mash or flatten them.
If you warm the berries in the microwave, stir well and check for hot spots.
Some oats are processed with wheat; check the label if you avoid gluten.
Make it fresh, and throw away what your baby doesn’t eat.

recipes.title: Zucchini and potato mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] A soft, mild first green vegetable, mashed with potato.

familyMeal.note: Steam a little zucchini for baby while you make your zucchini noodles.

ingredients: 1 small yellow or white potato, peeled and diced
1 small zucchini, ends trimmed and diced
A tiny pinch of mild cumin or nutritional yeast (optional)
steps: Steam the potato and zucchini together for about 10 minutes, until both are completely tender.
Mash together with a fork.
Stir in a tiny pinch of cumin or nutritional yeast if you like. Serve lukewarm.
tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Potato can turn grainy when frozen.

recipes.title: Butternut squash and apple puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Squash and sweet apple, steamed and blended smooth or mashed.

familyMeal.note: Steam extra squash to add to your own stew or soup.

ingredients: 1 small sweet apple, peeled, cored and chopped
steps: Steam the squash and apple for 12 to 15 minutes, until fork-tender.
Blend, or mash well with a fork for a chunkier texture, adding a little of the steaming water as needed. Let it cool before serving.
tips: Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Steamed broccoli and potato mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] A gentle introduction to green vegetables, mashed until creamy.

familyMeal.note: Steam a few extra broccoli florets for baby before you stir-fry the rest.

ingredients: 1 tsp breast milk, formula or water
steps: Steam the potato and broccoli together for 10 to 12 minutes, until very tender.
Mash with the breast milk, formula or water until smooth and creamy. Let it cool before serving.
tips: Broccoli is a good source of vitamin C, which helps your baby absorb iron from other foods.
Once your baby has had dairy, you can stir in 1 tsp unsalted butter instead; it contains milk.
Refrigerate for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Creamy pumpkin and cinnamon oatmeal
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Soft oats with pumpkin and a tiny pinch of cinnamon.

familyMeal.note: Make a pot of cinnamon porridge for yourself at the same time.

ingredients: 1/4 cup canned pure pumpkin (not pumpkin pie filling)
1/3 cup water, breast milk or formula
steps: Cook the oats in the water in a small pot over medium-low heat for about 4 minutes, until thick. If you’re using breast milk or formula, stir it in off the heat.
Stir in the pumpkin and cinnamon until warm and well mixed. Let it cool before serving.
tips: Check the can says 100% pumpkin; pie filling has added sugar and spices.
Some oats are processed with wheat; check the label if you avoid gluten.
Make it fresh, and throw away what your baby doesn’t eat.

recipes.title: Ripe pear and chia mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Soft pear with a little soaked chia for healthy fats.

familyMeal.note: Stir up a chia pudding for yourself tonight.

ingredients: 1 ripe, soft pear, peeled and cored
steps: Chop the pear. Steam it for about 5 minutes if it’s firm, or use it raw if it’s very ripe and soft.
Mash the pear well with a fork and stir in the chia.
Let it sit for about 15 minutes so the chia softens completely before serving.
tips: Use ground chia, or whole chia soaked until fully gel-like. Dry chia seeds swell with liquid and can clump.
Make it fresh, and throw away what your baby doesn’t eat.

recipes.title: Mango and Greek yogurt bowl
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Creamy yogurt swirled with smooth mango.

familyMeal.note: Make yourself a yogurt parfait with the rest of the mango.

ingredients: 1/4 cup ripe mango chunks, fresh or thawed frozen
steps: Mash the mango with a fork until smooth, or blend it.
Stir the mango into the yogurt until creamy. Serve cold or at room temperature.
tips: Yogurt adds protein and calcium. Choose plain yogurt with no added sugar.
Contains milk: offer yogurt once your baby has had dairy without a reaction.

recipes.title: Mashed banana and oatmeal
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Soft oats sweetened only with ripe banana.

familyMeal.note: Bake a tray of banana oatmeal cups for your own breakfasts.

ingredients: 1/3 cup water, breast milk or formula
steps: Cook the oats in the water in a small pot for 3 to 5 minutes, until soft. If you’re using breast milk or formula, stir it in off the heat.
Mash the banana with a fork and stir it into the warm oatmeal until smooth.
tips: Some oats are processed with wheat; check the label if you avoid gluten.
Make it fresh, and throw away what your baby doesn’t eat.

recipes.title: Zucchini and white bean mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Creamy white beans and soft zucchini for plant protein and fiber.

familyMeal.note: Toss the rest of the beans into your own salad for lunch.

ingredients: 1/2 cup canned cannellini beans (no salt added), rinsed and drained well
A splash of water or olive oil
steps: Steam the zucchini for 6 to 8 minutes, until tender.
Add the zucchini and beans to a bowl with a splash of water or olive oil, and mash until smooth and creamy, with no whole beans left.
tips: Whole beans are a choking hazard; mash every bean well.
Choose canned beans with no salt added, and rinse them well.
Refrigerate for up to 3 days.

recipes.title: Steamed apple and spinach puree
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Spinach blended with sweet apple into a smooth green puree.

familyMeal.note: Save some baby spinach for your own salad.

ingredients: 1 small apple, peeled, cored and chopped
steps: Steam the apple for 6 minutes, then add the spinach for the last 2 minutes until wilted.
Blend until smooth. Let it cool before serving.
tips: Spinach adds iron and folate; the vitamin C in apple helps your baby absorb the iron.
Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Sweet potato and peach mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Sweet potato and ripe peach, mashed together until smooth.

familyMeal.note: Roast extra sweet potato for your own quinoa bowls.

ingredients: 1/2 small sweet potato, peeled and diced
1 ripe peach, pitted and chopped, or thawed frozen peach slices
steps: Steam the sweet potato for 10 minutes, then add the peach for the last 3 minutes so it softens.
Mash together with a fork until smooth. Let it cool before serving.
tips: Peel the peach first if the skin is tough.
Refrigerate for up to 3 days, or freeze in cubes and use within 3 months.

recipes.title: Salmon and sweet potato mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Flaked salmon folded into a lumpy mash.

familyMeal.note: Bake one extra fillet with no lemon or seasoning, then flake it for baby, checking for bones.

ingredients: 1 medium sweet potato, peeled and cubed
steps: Bake the salmon at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 145°F.
Meanwhile, steam the sweet potato until very soft.
Remove every bone, flake the salmon finely and mash it into the sweet potato, leaving some soft lumps.
tips: Salmon is on the FDA's "Best Choices" list for low mercury.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly, and check for signs of spoilage before serving.

recipes.title: Soft veggie fingers
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Steamed carrot and zucchini sticks for little hands.

familyMeal.note: Steam a few carrot and zucchini sticks for baby before stir-frying the rest with soy sauce.

steps: Peel the carrot. Cut both vegetables into finger-length sticks.
Steam the carrot for about 12 minutes and the zucchini for about 5, until they squash easily between your fingers.
Cool before serving.
tips: Raw carrot is a choking hazard; always cook it until soft.
Stay with your baby while they eat.

recipes.title: Banana oat pancakes
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Three ingredients, cut into soft strips.

familyMeal.note: Same banana, oat and egg base: bake the oatmeal for the family and fry a few small pancakes for baby.

ingredients: A little oil for the pan
steps: Mash the banana, then mix in the egg and oats.
Cook small spoonfuls in a lightly oiled pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until set all the way through.
Cool and cut into thin strips.
tips: Ripe banana sweetens them; no sugar or honey needed.
Oats may be processed with wheat; check the label if you avoid gluten.

recipes.title: Tiny pasta with lentil tomato sauce
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Soft pasta in a smooth, no-salt-added sauce.

familyMeal.note: Both are tomato pasta nights: cook baby's pasta a little longer so it's very soft.

steps: Simmer the lentils, tomatoes and water for 20 minutes until the lentils are very soft, then blend smooth.
Cook the pasta until very soft, a few minutes longer than the package says.
Stir the pasta into the sauce and cut any larger pieces small.
tips: Choose canned tomatoes labeled no salt added.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly, and check for signs of spoilage before serving.

recipes.title: Flaked salmon and cream cheese mash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Soft salmon folded into creamy potato, with gentle chunks to explore.

familyMeal.note: Set aside a piece of plain salmon for baby before you season the family’s.

ingredients: 1 small cooked salmon fillet, skin and bones removed
1 small potato, peeled, boiled and mashed
1 tbsp plain cream cheese or whole-milk Greek yogurt
steps: Flake the salmon with a fork, checking carefully for any bones.
Stir the salmon into the warm mashed potato with the cream cheese until creamy, with soft chunks.
tips: Cook salmon to 145°F, until it flakes easily.
Salmon is on the FDA’s "Best Choices" list for children.
Refrigerate for up to 2 days.

recipes.title: Steamed carrot and zucchini "fries" with yogurt dip
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Soft veggie sticks for self-feeding, with a creamy yogurt dip.

familyMeal.note: Steam extra veggie sticks for your own snack plate.

ingredients: 1 medium carrot, peeled and cut into finger-sized sticks
1 small zucchini, cut into finger-sized sticks
A tiny pinch of garlic powder
steps: Steam the carrot and zucchini sticks for 8 to 12 minutes, until soft enough to squash between your thumb and finger.
Stir the garlic powder into the yogurt.
Serve the sticks lukewarm with the yogurt on the side for dipping.
tips: Pediatric guidance suggests finger foods soft enough to squash easily between your thumb and finger.
Raw or firm carrot is a choking hazard; always cook it soft.
Always stay with your baby while they eat, and have them sit upright.

recipes.title: Cheesy broccoli and quinoa bites
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] Soft mini muffins with quinoa, broccoli, cheese and egg.

familyMeal.note: Bake a tray of veggie egg muffins for yourself at the same time.

steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and lightly grease a mini muffin tin.
Mix the quinoa, broccoli, cheese and egg.
Spoon into the muffin cups and bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until set all the way through.
Let them cool completely before serving.

recipes.title: Deconstructed turkey and lentil chili
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] One pot of turkey and lentil chili: spiced and topped for you, mildly seasoned as crumbles or a fork mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: chunky chili of ground turkey, lentils, tomatoes and bell peppers, seasoned with chili powder and sea salt and topped with cheddar and cilantro. Take baby’s portion out before adding chili powder and salt.

steps: Brown the turkey in a large pot, breaking it up finely, until cooked through to 165°F.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, bell pepper, water, cumin and garlic powder. Simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until the lentils are very soft.
Spoon out baby’s portion before adding any chili powder or salt.
For finger food: offer soft turkey crumbles and soft lentils for pincer-grasp practice.
For a mash: lightly mash turkey, lentils and stewed tomatoes with a fork.
Season the rest with chili powder and salt and top with cheddar and cilantro.
tips: Lentils and turkey are sources of iron.
Cool baby’s portion before serving, and freeze extra in small containers.

recipes.title: Sheet-pan roasted chicken, zucchini and squash
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] One tray of chicken thighs and summer squash: herby and crisp-skinned for you, as soft spears and shredded chicken for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: skin-on chicken thighs, zucchini and yellow squash roasted with olive oil, Italian seasoning, garlic powder and sea salt. Season baby’s corner of the tray with olive oil and herbs only.

steps: Cut the zucchini and squash into long spears and toss with olive oil and herbs.
Keep baby’s chicken and spears on one corner of the tray, unsalted.
Roast at 425°F for 35 to 40 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F and the vegetables are very soft.
For finger food: peel baby’s spears and serve with shredded tender thigh meat, skin removed.
For a mash: finely shred chicken thigh and mash it with soft roasted zucchini.
Season the grown-up portions with sea salt.
tips: Remove chicken skin and any bones before serving baby.
Finger-squish test: many parents check that any vegetable or protein served as finger food squishes easily between their thumb and index finger.

recipes.title: Slow-cooked beef and root vegetable stew
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] One pot of slow-braised beef with carrots, potatoes and parsnips: seasoned at the table for you, shredded or mashed for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: tender chuck roast braised with carrots, potatoes, parsnips, rosemary and garlic in beef broth, seasoned to taste at the table.

ingredients: 3 cups low-sodium or no-salt-added beef broth
steps: Brown the beef in a heavy pot, then add the garlic, rosemary, vegetables and broth.
Cover and braise at 325°F (or on low in a slow cooker) for about 3 hours, until the beef shreds easily.
For finger food: shred baby’s beef very finely with a fork and serve with soft potato and carrot wedges.
For a mash: mash potato, carrot and shredded beef with a spoonful of warm broth.
Let the grown-ups season their bowls with salt and pepper at the table.
tips: Beef is a source of iron.
Remove the rosemary sprig before serving baby.

recipes.title: Creamy butternut squash and ricotta pasta
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] One pot of squash and ricotta pasta: with parmesan and pepper for you, as sauce-coated rigatoni or a dipping puree for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: rigatoni or penne tossed in a sauce of pureed butternut squash, ricotta, nutmeg and garlic, finished with parmesan, salt and black pepper. Set baby’s portion aside before adding salt and parmesan.

steps: Steam or roast the squash with the garlic until very soft, then blend with the ricotta and nutmeg.
Cook the rigatoni until soft, a little past al dente for baby.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and set baby’s portion aside before adding salt or parmesan.
For finger food: serve large, well-cooked rigatoni coated in the sauce.
For a mash: mash the pasta slightly, or serve the sauce as a thick dip on a pre-loaded spoon.
Finish the grown-up bowls with parmesan, salt and black pepper.
tips: Dairy and wheat are common allergens. Introduce each one on its own first before combining them in family meals.
Large pasta shapes like rigatoni are easier for little hands than small ones.

recipes.title: Baked white fish with cauliflower and potato
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] One bake of cod with cauliflower and potato: lemon butter and parmesan mash for you, as soft flakes and florets or a smooth mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: cod or halibut baked with lemon butter and fresh dill, over garlic-parmesan mashed potatoes and steamed cauliflower.

ingredients: 2 to 3 boneless cod or halibut fillets
Breast milk or formula, to thin
steps: Bake the fish at 400°F for 12 to 15 minutes, until it flakes easily and reaches 145°F. Keep baby’s fillet plain.
Boil the potatoes and steam the cauliflower until very soft.
For finger food: flake baby’s fish, checking for bones, and serve with soft cauliflower florets.
For a mash: mash plain potato and cauliflower with flaked fish and a splash of breast milk, formula or olive oil.
Make the grown-up mash with garlic, parmesan, butter and salt, and finish the fish with lemon butter and dill.
tips: Always double-check flaked fish for small bones.
Fish is a common allergen. Introduce each one on its own first before combining them in family meals.

recipes.title: Mild coconut chicken curry
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] One pot of mild coconut curry: over brown rice for you, as sauce-coated chicken strips or a golden mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: chicken strips simmered in full-fat coconut milk with turmeric, ginger, garlic, sweet peas and bell peppers, over brown rice. Add chili and salt to the grown-up pot after baby’s portion is out.

ingredients: 1 lb chicken breast, cut into strips
1 red bell pepper, in long strips
steps: Roast the bell pepper strips at 400°F until very soft.
Soften the garlic and ginger, stir in the turmeric, then add the chicken and coconut milk and simmer until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Stir in the peas for the last 5 minutes. Scoop out baby’s portion before adding salt or chili.
For finger food: serve soft chicken strips coated in sauce with the soft roasted pepper strips.
For a mash: blend chicken, peas and brown rice with a little sauce into a golden mash.
Season the rest and serve over brown rice.
tips: Mash or flatten peas for babies: whole peas can be a choking risk.
Scoop before seasoning: take baby’s portion out before adding salt, soy sauce, hot pepper or other spicy seasoning.

recipes.title: Italian beef and zucchini meatballs
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] One batch of baked beef and zucchini meatballs: in marinara over spaghetti for you, as soft strips or a mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: baked beef and zucchini meatballs simmered in marinara and served over spaghetti. Mix a little salt into the grown-up batch only.

ingredients: 1 zucchini, finely grated and squeezed dry
steps: Mix the beef, zucchini, breadcrumbs, egg, garlic powder and oregano. Shape baby’s portion first, with no added salt.
Bake at 400°F for 18 to 20 minutes, until cooked through to 160°F.
For finger food: cut baby’s meatballs into strips or quarters. Never serve whole round meatballs to a young baby.
For a mash: mash a meatball with a little low-sodium tomato sauce or warm water.
Simmer the grown-up meatballs in marinara and serve over spaghetti.
tips: Egg and wheat are common allergens. Introduce each one on its own first before combining them in family meals.
Shape baby’s portion into small logs instead of balls for easier, safer grabbing.

recipes.title: Tofu, broccoli and sesame noodle bowl
recipes.summary: [PLACEHOLDER - needs expert review] One bowl of tofu, broccoli and noodles: in a sesame-peanut sauce with chili for you, as soft strips or a mash for baby.

familyMeal.note: Mama’s plate: pan-seared tofu cubes, steamed broccoli and noodles tossed in a sesame-peanut sauce with soy sauce, lime and chili flakes. Add soy sauce and chili to the grown-up portion only.

steps: Bake plain tofu strips at 400°F for 20 minutes, until set but soft. Steam the broccoli until very soft and cook the noodles until soft.
Thin the peanut butter and tahini with warm water into a smooth, runny sauce.
For finger food: serve long strips of soft tofu, broccoli florets and soft noodles coated in a little of the thinned sauce.
For a mash: mash soft tofu and broccoli heads with a drop of warm water or thinned peanut butter.
Toss the grown-up bowls with the rest of the sauce, soy sauce, lime and chili flakes.
tips: Peanut, sesame, soy and wheat are common allergens. Introduce each one on its own first before combining them in family meals.
Always thin nut and seed butters: a thick spoonful is a choking risk.
